transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Reyes (Fieldstone Dir ML Ops), Tom Keller (Fieldstone Platform Eng), Ari Voss (Fieldstone Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete): Kickoff to align on go-live runway and technical intake for Fieldstone's first production workload on Redwood.

[00:00] Lena Park: Alright, hi everyone. Welcome, thanks for carving time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE for Fieldstone. Omar's with me, he's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya Reyes: Hey Lena, doing good. Thanks. Excited to get this rolling.
[00:14] Tom Keller: Hi all, Tom here. Want to make sure we can hit our latency SLAs for the new insights pipeline.
[00:20] Omar Singh: Yeah, hi. Quick intro from my side — I run infra perf at Redwood, will lead the benchmark and the runbook for the pilot.
[00:28] Ari Voss: Ari here. I'll be driving the security checklist. We'll focus on KMS integration and audit trails.
[00:35] Lena Park: Great. Agenda for today: 1) clarify success criteria and timeline, 2) walk constraints — network, data residency, compliance, 3) go over a proposed onboarding plan and benchmark, and 4) agree next steps. Any additions?
[00:47] Maya Reyes: Nope that covers it. Perhaps also touch on cost targets — we have pretty tight compute budgets this quarter.
[00:54] Lena Park: Absolutely, we'll cover cost per 1k tokens and batching recommendations.

[01:10] -- Topic: Success criteria and timeline --
[01:12] Lena Park: So Maya, can you share the top three success metrics for this pilot?
[01:18] Maya Reyes: Sure. Number one, p99 latency needs to be under 400ms for single-request RPCs at our expected load. Two: cost per 1k tokens we want to be below $0.07 if possible. And three: fully private network—traffic must stay in our VPC, no egress to public internet.
[01:33] Omar Singh: Understood. Quick note: private network is doable via our Redwood Private flow, but there are two approaches — a managed private control plane with VPC peering, or a full on-prem package if you need air-gap.
[01:45] Tom Keller: We're leaning toward VPC peering with customer-managed subnets. Less ops overhead for us.
[01:51] Ari Voss: We'll need KMS integration with our HSM provider, and recording of audit logs for every inference request — retention for 2 years. Also SSO/SCIM for RBAC is non-negotiable.
[02:04] Lena Park: Good, we support KMS integrations and have an audit log pipeline. Omar will flag any edge cases.

[03:00] -- Topic: Deployment flavor tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private) --
[03:05] Omar Singh: Quick sketch: hosted API is fastest to spin up but doesn't satisfy VPC-only restrictions. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput. Private VPC gives you private network and KMS control but needs more setup, like peering and security review.
[03:20] Tom Keller: Latency-wise, dedicated and private are similar if they're colocated. Our concern is warmup and KV cache priming — we have bursts of long sequences.
[03:31] Omar Singh: Right, KV cache behavior matters. For bursts, we'd recommend pinned model instances with steady-state warm caches or custom batching policies. We'll propose autoscaling knobs in the runbook.
[03:45] Maya Reyes: How do you handle model rollouts? We need canary to test prompts before global switch.
[03:50] Lena Park: We support canary rollouts and staged A/B. You can pin a percentage to new model versions and fallback automatically if quality drops. We also tie regressions to eval sets so we can halt a rollout automatically.

[05:10] -- Topic: Performance benchmarking and data needed --
[05:12] Omar Singh: For the benchmark we'll need a sample traffic dump: typical prompt length, 95th and 99th percentile token lengths, request rate distribution over an hour. Tom, can you export that?
[05:22] Tom Keller: Yep, I can get a sample. We have a preprocessing step that truncates to 1024 but some sequences hit 4k. Should I include the raw distribution?
[05:30] Omar Singh: Yes raw distribution helps. Also include any rate-limiting spikes — e.g., 2-minute bursts. We'll run steady-state and burst tests.
[05:39] Lena Park: For cost modeling, include number of tokens per request and expected daily volume.

[06:15] Maya Reyes: Quick question about quantization — we saw notes about 4-bit and 8-bit options. How does that impact quality?
[06:22] Omar Singh: Good question. 4-bit quantization reduces memory and cost but can slightly affect generation quality for some models and longer contexts. For your workload with long sequences we might recommend a mixed approach — quantize embeddings or smaller-head layers but keep attention and KV paths higher fidelity. We'll propose a quantization profile with expected QPS vs quality tradeoffs.

[07:30] -- Topic: Security and compliance --
[07:32] Ari Voss: We're running the security checklist. Two items: KMS—our key policy requires non-exportable keys with HSM-backed wrapping, and audit logs must be tamper-evident. Also need SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:46] Lena Park: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, CloudHSM). Our audit logs are immutable and exportable to S3 or your SIEM. For SAML and SCIM we support SSO + SCIM provisioning for RBAC.
[07:58] Ari Voss: Any data residency concerns? We need all inference compute in us-east-1 and no backups outside region.
[08:03] Omar Singh: We can pin region and enforce storage residency. We'll note retention and replica policies in the runbook.

[09:10] Tom Keller: One more ops question — how do you surface token-level billing and tracing? We need per-route cost attribution to our microservices.
[09:20] Lena Park: Redwood Console provides per-route token and cost breakdown, and we can add tracing hooks to correlate requests to your request IDs. We'll include an example tracing header in the runbook.

[10:45] -- Mid-call clarifying tangent / small crosstalk --
[10:46] Maya Reyes: Sorry, just—are there limits on concurrent connections per model?
[10:50] Omar Singh: We set soft limits but can reserve concurrency in Dedicated. For private we can size pools accordingly.
[10:55] Tom Keller: Ok cool.

[12:00] -- Onboarding plan walkthrough --
[12:05] Lena Park: Proposed 4-week runway: Week 0: intake and environment setup; Week 1: benchmark and perf tuning; Week 2: security integration and canary; Week 3: ramp and go-live. We'll provide runnable IaC bits for peering, sample configs, and a debugging checklist.
[12:25] Tom Keller: Is there a prebuilt Terraform module for the VPC peering and route tables?
[12:29] Omar Singh: Yes we have Terraform and CloudFormation templates. We'll share them and a small walkthrough doc.

[13:55] Maya Reyes: Who's our CSM? Is there a single point of contact during onboarding?
[14:00] Lena Park: You'll be assigned a CSM. For technical questions, Omar will be the SE lead. I'll coordinate kickoff and contract items.

[15:20] -- Budget and pricing discussion --
[15:22] Tom Keller: On the pricing model, can you give an example of cost under a dedicated scenario for 100k tokens/day?
[15:30] Lena Park: We'll run numbers after we see your token distribution but as a ballpark we can model reserved capacity discounts with predictable monthly commits. We'll include example TCO tables in the sheet I'll send.
[15:40] Tom Keller: Need those by mid next week for budget planning.
[15:43] Lena Park: We'll target 2026-06-15 for the pricing and runbook.

[18:00] -- Technical deep-dive snippets --
[18:05] Omar Singh: Small note on KV cache priming: if you have stateful sessions, you get large initial spikes. We recommend prefix caching and warmup endpoints to amortize token cost. Also continuous batching can help during bursts but might add a few ms tail latency.
[18:20] Tom Keller: That's important. We do chatty multi-turn sessions, so warm caches will be key.

[21:30] Maya Reyes: Regarding audits, does Redwood provide request-level hashes for non-repudiation?
[21:34] Omar Singh: We emit request IDs and cryptographic digests for logged payloads. You'll get immutable logs and can forward to your SIEM.

[24:00] -- Questions from customer --
[24:05] Tom Keller: If we need to swap models mid-flight because of a bug, how quick is rollback?
[24:10] Lena Park: Rollback is near-instant for canaryed models; we maintain fast failover policies. We can also configure automated fallback to a smaller, cheaper variant if latency balloons.

[27:40] Ari Voss: What about retention of prompt text in logs? We want payload minimization.
[27:45] Lena Park: You can configure redaction and token-level retention policies in Redwood Console; by default we store metadata and hashes, not full prompts unless you opt in. We'll include recommended defaults.

[31:00] -- Planning the benchmark run --
[31:05] Omar Singh: Proposing two benchmark runs: 1) steady-state for 30 minutes at expected QPS; 2) burst test with 2-minute spikes. We'll run multi-model variants and compare p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost per 1k tokens.
[31:22] Tom Keller: Agreed. Also include a long-context test up to 4k tokens.
[31:26] Omar Singh: Will do. I'll provide the harness and a dockerized client you can run against a staging endpoint.

[34:10] Maya Reyes: For the actual pilot, who signs off on go/no-go? Is it product or platform?
[34:15] Lena Park: Typically Platform owns performance sign-off, Product owns quality. We can formalize a checklist — we'll add it to the runbook.

[36:00] -- Recap and open items --
[36:05] Lena Park: Quick recap: we'll send the onboarding checklist and Terraform templates, Omar will run benchmark harness once you supply traffic samples, Ari to review security docs, and Lena will send pricing scenarios by 2026-06-15.
[36:20] Tom Keller: Sounds good. Please also include an example tracing header so we can wire request IDs.
[36:25] Omar Singh: Yep, I'll add that.

[38:00] Maya Reyes: Any other blockers? Not from our side.
[38:05] Ari Voss: None right now. We'll come back with KMS and retention specifics.

[41:10] Lena Park: Ok last thing — doc links. I'll email: onboarding runbook, Terraform templates, pricing sheet, and the benchmark harness repo link. I'll also include a short video walkthrough for the runbook.
[41:25] Tom Keller: Appreciate that.

[45:00] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps.
[45:06] Maya Reyes: Thanks Lena, Omar. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[45:10] Tom Keller: Bye all.
[45:12] Omar Singh: Bye.

End of transcript.
